_comment: Per-chart narratives. CI (build_prompt.py -> GitHub Models -> write_narrative.py) overwrites these from live numbers; this committed copy is the fallback so the page always reads well. source = 'fallback' | 'github-models'.

notes.basket: The breakfast basket, an index averaging prices of coffee, sugar, wheat, and orange juice relative to 2015 (base = 100), currently stands at 132, indicating a 32% increase since then. This rise reflects a recent and uneven climb across the underlying commodities rather than a steady trend. The index aggregates these key soft commodities globally, highlighting overall price pressure in this segment. Though the basket shows a notable increase, the variation among the components is significant.
notes.movers: Coffee has been the main driver, up 93% since 2015, followed by orange juice with a 22% increase. Wheat and sugar prices have risen more modestly, by 7% and 5% respectively. These price moves are largely due to weather-related disruptions and crop diseases—such as frost and drought affecting coffee arabica regions and citrus greening combined with hurricanes impacting orange juice production. The soft commodity markets involved are relatively thin, meaning supply shocks can cause sharp price swings rather than reflecting broad-based inflationary pressure.
notes.why: The headline rise in the breakfast basket is primarily driven by a few crops that are highly exposed to weather and disease risks rather than general inflation trends. Because these soft commodities are sensitive to climatic and biological factors, elevated prices can persist for several years. Market thinness amplifies the price impacts of such supply disruptions, contributing to sustained elevated levels.
